headline: Bharat Rasayan Limited: SEBI Takeover Disclosure under Regulation 10(5)
sum: Bharat Rasayan Limited filed a Regulation 10(5) disclosure under the SEBI Takeover Regulations, indicating a substantial acquisition of shares event. Full transaction details (acquiring party, stake, consideration, open offer trigger) remain restricted to the NSE filing.
implication: Regulation 10(5) disclosures are triggered by acquirers crossing 5% or more of shareholding; this filing marks the formal intimation to the exchange and market, and may trigger a mandatory open offer under Regulation 20 depending on the stake acquired.
detail: Bharat Rasayan submitted the Regulation 10(5) disclosure to NSE on 17 Aug 2026, confirming a substantial acquisition event. Regulation 10(5) requires disclosure within 2 business days of crossing thresholds (typically 5%, 10%, 15%, etc.). The identity of the acquirer, exact stake percentage, acquisition price, and whether a mandatory open offer will be triggered are contained in the filed document but cannot be corroborated from public press/regulatory summaries available.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Regulation 10(5)
framework.note: Disclosure of acquisition within 2 days of crossing 5% or higher thresholds; central gatekeeping mechanism for M&A in listed companies

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations, 2011 – Regulation 20 (Mandatory Open Offer)
framework.note: Typically triggered if acquirer holds 25% or more after the acquisition; conditions precedent to full control

Clarifies whether transaction is covered (e.g., issue of new shares, intra-group transfers may be exempt)

framework.note: Continuous disclosure and announcement obligations for material acquisition events

framework.note: If combined enterprise value > ₹3,000 cr or other thresholds, CCI pre-approval may be gating

conditions: Completion of 5% or higher threshold acquisition
